APT-ENG-0851: The error lies in segment (A) 'The students usually asks'. The subject 'The students' is plural and takes the plural verb 'ask', not the third-person singular inflected form 'asks'. Correct sentence: 'The students usually ask for a bonus time of thirty minutes for completing their projects.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0852: The error lies in segment (A) 'that King Lear confided to'. The verb 'confide' meaning to impart secrets or entrust private feelings to someone takes the preposition 'in' ('confided in his daughter'), not 'to'. Correct sentence: 'There was no denying the fact that King Lear confided in his daughter Cordelia more than anybody else.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0853: The error lies in segment (C) 'aimed highly'. In the idiom 'aim high', 'high' serves as a flat adverb of direction and ambition; 'highly' means favorably or greatly and does not modify 'aim'. Correct sentence: 'He always aimed high in life.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0854: There is no grammatical error in this sentence. 'And it just recently awarded a million-dollar contract that reeks of corruption' is syntactically sound, idiomatic, and correct. Hence, option D ('No error') is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0855: There is no grammatical error in this sentence. 'The Event Horizon Telescope can help scientists analyse the shapes and behaviours of event horizons' correctly uses the bare infinitive 'analyse' after 'help' and proper plural agreement. Hence, option B ('No error') is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0856: The error lies in segment (A) 'In course by time,'. The established prepositional idiom expressing progression through time is 'In course of time', not 'by time'. Correct sentence: 'In course of time, he was wise enough to realise the mistakes of his past life.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0857: The error lies in segment (C) 'a boiling temperature, were putting wildlife populations at peril'. The sentence specifies ongoing modern environmental challenges ('The present-century threats'), requiring the present continuous tense 'are putting' rather than the past tense 'were putting'. Correct sentence: '...are putting wildlife populations at peril.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0858: Option C correctly rectifies the error. In the future perfect continuous construction ('will have been + V-ing'), the auxiliary following the modal 'will' must appear in its base form 'have', not the third-person inflected form 'has'. Correct sentence: 'In 2023, she will have been working in the company for three years.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0859: The error lies in segment (D) 'patterns are made more scarcer, other'. 'Scarcer' is already the comparative degree of 'scarce'; preceding it with 'more' forms an erroneous double comparative. Correct sentence: '...patterns are made scarcer, other arrangements and patterns will spring up.' Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0860: The error lies in segment (B) 'based at'. The participial preposition meaning determined or founded on something is 'based on', not 'based at'. Correct sentence: 'Employees were given incentives based on their performance.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0861: The error lies in segment (C) 'it has turned sour'. A zero conditional describing a universal physical or chemical reaction takes the simple present tense in both clauses: 'If a few drops of lemon are put in the milk, it turns sour.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0862: The error lies in segment (C) 'did not wanted'. Following the auxiliary 'did not', the main verb must appear in its base form (bare infinitive V1 'want'), not the past tense 'wanted'. Correct sentence: 'The old man did not want to eat any food.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0863: The error lies in option D 'have'. When treated as a single unified competitive sports unit, the collective noun 'team' in formal English takes the singular auxiliary verb 'has won', not 'have'. Correct sentence: 'Our team has won the match.' Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0864: The error lies in segment (A) 'leave behind'. The participle clause expressing the consequence of the cyclone's movement requires the present participle 'leaving behind', not the base form 'leave behind'. Correct sentence: 'Cyclone Amphan roared into West Bengal on Wednesday leaving behind a trail of devastation...' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0865: The error lies in segment (D) 'someone has been picked my pocket'. The subject 'someone' actively committed the theft, requiring the present perfect active construction 'has picked my pocket', not the passive form 'has been picked'. Correct sentence: 'I think someone has picked my pocket while I was travelling in the metro.' Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0866: The error lies in segment (A) 'were warning'. The children were the recipients of the caution in the passive voice, which requires the past participle 'were warned', not the active participle 'were warning'. Correct sentence: 'The children were warned not to try to climb the cliffs as they were very steep.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0867: The error lies in option D 'complains for'. The verb 'complain' collocates with the preposition 'about' or 'of' when expressing dissatisfaction regarding an issue ('complains about the noise'), not 'for'. Correct sentence: 'My neighbor constantly complains about the noise coming from the children playing in the park.' Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0868: The error lies in segment (A) 'take a sharpest turn'. An indefinite article 'a' cannot be paired with a superlative adjective ('sharpest'); it should either be 'take a sharp turn' (positive degree) or 'take the sharpest turn' (superlative with definite article). Correct sentence: '...go straight and then take a sharp turn towards your left...' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0869: The error lies in segment (D) 'in bush.'. The traditional English proverb requires the definite article before the singular countable noun 'bush': 'A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush.' Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0870: The error lies in part (2) 'than me'. The Latin comparative adjective 'senior' takes the preposition 'to', not 'than'. Correct sentence: 'He is senior to me.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0871: The error lies in part (2) 'were chosen'. The distributive pronoun 'Neither' is singular and takes the singular verb 'was chosen'. Correct sentence: 'Neither of the two candidates was chosen.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0872: The error lies in part (2) 'who has'. The relative pronoun 'who' refers to the plural antecedent 'those', requiring the plural verb 'have'. Correct sentence: 'She is one of those who have contributed.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0873: There is no grammatical error in this sentence. 'Hardly had the game started when it began to rain' correctly uses past perfect subject-auxiliary inversion and the correlative conjunction 'when'. Hence, option D ('No error') is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0874: The error lies in part (2) 'on to accompany'. The verb 'insist' takes the preposition 'on' followed by a gerund ('insisted on accompanying'), not an infinitive. Correct sentence: 'He insisted on accompanying her.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0875: The error lies in part (2) 'applicants have decreased'. The phrase 'The number of + plural noun' takes a singular verb ('has decreased'). Correct sentence: 'The number of applicants has decreased.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0876: The error lies in part (2) 'than her peers'. Comparative adjectives ending in '-ior' take the preposition 'to', not 'than'. Correct sentence: 'She is junior to her peers.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0877: The error lies in part (2) 'were rewarded'. When subjects joined by 'and' are each preceded by 'each', the verb is singular ('was rewarded'). Correct sentence: 'Each boy and girl was rewarded.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0878: The error lies in part (2) 'when the whistle blew'. The correlative pair with 'No sooner' is 'than', not 'when'. Correct sentence: 'No sooner did the train arrive than the whistle blew.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0879: The error lies in part (2) 'police has caught'. The collective noun 'police' is plural and takes the plural auxiliary 'have caught'. Correct sentence: 'The police have caught the thief.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0880: The error lies in part (1) 'Unless you do not hurry'. 'Unless' has an inherent negative meaning ('if not'); pairing it with 'do not' creates an erroneous double negative. Correct sentence: 'Unless you hurry, you will be late.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0881: The error lies in part (2) 'prefer tea than coffee'. The verb 'prefer' takes the preposition 'to', not 'than'. Correct sentence: 'I prefer tea to coffee.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0882: The error lies in part (2) 'Bread and butter are a healthy breakfast'. When two items joined by 'and' represent a single composite meal, the verb is singular ('is a healthy breakfast'). Correct sentence: 'Bread and butter is a healthy breakfast.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0883: The error lies in part (2) 'One of the student'. 'One of the + plural noun' requires 'students'. Correct sentence: 'One of the students is missing.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0884: The error lies in part (1) 'She don't know'. The third-person singular pronoun 'She' takes 'doesn't know', not 'don't know'. Correct sentence: 'She doesn't know the answer.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0885: The error lies in part (2) 'is because'. The expression 'The reason why... is because' is redundant; the correct copular complement is 'is that...'. Correct sentence: 'The reason why he failed is that he was careless.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0886: The error lies in segment (C) 'A great'. The specific culture of hospitality associated with the Spanish nation takes the definite article 'The great culture', not 'A great'. Correct sentence: 'The great culture of hospitality of the Spanish is well-known.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0887: The error lies in segment (D) 'He part the grass'. The narrative is set in the past ('had seen'), requiring the simple past tense 'parted' rather than the base form 'part'. Correct sentence: 'He parted the grass at the place where he had seen the deer.' Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0888: The error lies in segment (A) 'but returned back'. The verb 'return' already means 'to go or come back'; using 'back' is an erroneous pleonasm. Correct sentence: 'He went to work but returned immediately.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0889: The error lies in segment (D) 'still 10 p.m.'. When expressing a time interval introduced by 'from', the preposition denoting the end of the span is 'to' or 'until' ('from 10 a.m. to 10 p.m.'), not 'still'. Correct sentence: 'The supermarket is open from 10 a.m. to 10 p.m.' Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0890: The error lies in segment (C) 'good with running'. The idiom for expressing skill or proficiency in a sport or activity is 'good at' followed by a gerund ('good at running'), not 'good with'. Correct sentence: 'Deepa and Seema are both good at running...' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0891: Option A provides the correct sentence. The original sentence contained a redundant second auxiliary verb ('Is Savita is joining...'). Option A correctly states: 'Is Savita joining us for lunch today?' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0892: The error lies in segment (D) 'is led to'. The construction has actively produced the population increase; the present perfect active 'has led to' must be used rather than the passive 'is led to'. Correct sentence: 'The construction of the new business school has led to a sudden rise of population in our area.' Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0893: The error lies in part (2) 'are traveling to the international conference'. When a singular subject ('The CEO') is joined to another noun by 'along with', the verb agrees strictly with the first subject, requiring the singular verb 'is traveling', not 'are traveling'. Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0894: The error lies in part (2) 'new group of interns'. The singular countable noun phrase 'new group' requires the indefinite article 'a': 'a new group of interns'. Correct sentence: 'The company plans to hire a new group of interns...' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0895: The error lies in segment (C) 'consequency, we had'. The word 'consequency' is non-standard; the appropriate conjunctive adverb indicating result is 'consequently'. Correct sentence: 'The project was delayed because of unforeseen issues; consequently, we had to adjust our timeline.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0896: The error lies in part (3) 'have caused significant strain'. The grammatical subject of the sentence is the singular noun 'The sudden influx', which takes the singular verb 'has caused', not the plural 'have caused'. Correct sentence: 'The sudden influx of tourists... has caused significant strain on the local infrastructure.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0897: The error lies in segment (B) 'It was a surprising'. 'Surprising' is a participial adjective that cannot take the indefinite article 'a' without a noun; it should be the noun phrase 'It was a surprise' or the predicate adjective 'It was surprising' (without 'a'). Correct sentence: 'It was a surprise to receive the gift from my brother.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0898: The error lies in segment (A) 'The monkeys swinged'. The simple past tense of the irregular verb 'swing' is 'swung', not 'swinged'. Correct sentence: 'The monkeys swung on the branches and jumped over the compound wall.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0899: The error lies in segment (A) 'They secret'. The verb 'decided' must be modified by an adverb of manner ('secretly'), not an adjective ('secret'). Correct sentence: 'They secretly decided to leave the town.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0900: The error lies in segment (A) 'has repeated asked him'. The verb 'asked' must be modified by an adverb of frequency/manner ('repeatedly'), not the adjective/participle 'repeated'. Correct sentence: 'Deepu’s mother has repeatedly asked him to lower the volume of his mobile.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0901: The error lies in segment (D) 'are being honoured'. Two professional designations referring to the same individual (indicated by a single definite article 'The famous author and actor') form a singular subject and take the singular verb 'is being honoured', not the plural 'are'. Correct sentence: 'The famous author and actor is being honoured at a function today.' Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0902: The error lies in segment (B) 'point at'. The verb 'concede' takes the preposition 'to' when yielding or granting an advantage to an opponent ('conceded a crucial point to his opponent'), not 'at'. Correct sentence: 'He conceded a very crucial point to his opponent.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0903: The error lies in segment (C) 'to sold their land'. After the infinitive particle 'to', the verb must appear in its base form (bare infinitive V1 'sell'), not the past tense 'sold'. Correct sentence: 'Raman went with his wife to the village to sell their land.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0904: The error lies in segment (A) 'from one generation through a next'. The standard correlative prepositional idiom denoting generational transmission is 'from one generation to the next', not 'through a next'. Correct sentence: 'Mithila art tradition is passed on from one generation to the next...' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0905: The error lies in segment (B) 'I get myself tired'. In English, 'get tired' is an intransitive copular expression; adding the reflexive pronoun 'myself' is ungrammatical. Correct sentence: 'I find that I get tired very easily these days.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0906: The error lies in segment (C) 'but you will get wet'. The coordinating conjunction 'but' expresses contrast, whereas the clause warns of an undesirable result if the action is not taken; the proper conjunction is 'otherwise' or 'or'. Correct sentence: 'It's raining heavily, so you should take an umbrella, or you will get wet.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0907: The error lies in option D 'from darkness'. The adjective 'afraid' takes the preposition 'of', not 'from' ('afraid of darkness'). Correct sentence: 'As a little child she was afraid of darkness.' Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0908: The error lies in segment (A) 'with a rich heiress'. In the active voice, the verb 'marry' is transitive and takes a direct object without the preposition 'with'. Correct sentence: 'He married a rich heiress last year.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0909: The error lies in segment (A) 'what I buy'. The relative pronoun referring to 'The present' must be 'that' or 'which' (not 'what'), and the past time marker 'yesterday' requires the simple past tense 'bought'. Correct sentence: 'The present that I bought for you yesterday was very expensive.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0910: The error lies in part (2) 'more effective than the previous coach'. The sentence makes an illogical comparison between 'The training programme' and 'the previous coach' (a person); it must compare the programme with 'that of the previous coach' or 'the previous coach's'. Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0911: The error lies in segment (B) 'Are today'. The noun 'today' is singular and takes the singular copular verb 'Is', not the plural 'Are'. Correct sentence: 'Is today a working day or a holiday?' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0912: The error lies in segment (D) 'but he bring'. The narrative is set in the past ('was blind'), requiring the simple past tense 'brought' rather than the base form 'bring'. Correct sentence: 'My guide was blind but he brought me home safely.' Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0913: The error lies in part (1) 'The proposal seeks to neither expand existing facilities'. Parallelism with 'neither... nor' requires balancing parallel verb phrases: 'The proposal seeks neither to expand existing facilities nor to hire additional staff members' or 'seeks to neither expand... nor hire'. Part (1) contains the misplaced correlative conjunction. Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0914: The error lies in segment (A) 'went to school'. Following the auxiliary 'did not', the main verb must appear in its base form (bare infinitive V1 'go'), not the past tense 'went'. Correct sentence: 'Mohan did not go to school yesterday as he was unwell.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0915: The error lies in segment (C) 'She behaves in a'. The double indefinite article construction 'in a such a' is grammatically incorrect; the proper phrasing is 'in such a cordial manner'. Correct sentence: 'She behaves in such a cordial manner that everyone admires her.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0916: The error lies in part (2) 'then the power went out'. The negative adverb 'barely' pairs with the conjunction 'when' or 'before', not 'then'. Correct sentence: 'She had barely finished writing her essay when the power went out...' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0917: The error lies in part (3) 'have reignited debates'. The grammatical subject of the sentence is the singular noun 'The emergence', which takes the singular auxiliary verb 'has reignited', not the plural 'have reignited'. Correct sentence: 'The emergence of new infectious variants... has reignited debates on public health preparedness...' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
